issues.failure_explanation: The proof's intermediate inequality bounds |1-f(x)| by |1-x^2|^((d+1)^T)/(1+f(x)), but the correct Padé composition error bound carries exponent (q+1)^T where d = 2q+1. For d = 3 (q = 1), T = 1, x = 0.5: |1-p(0.5)| = 0.3125 exceeds 0.75^4/1.6875 ≈ 0.1875, so the inequality with (d+1)^T = 4 is false. With exponent (q+1)^T = 2 the bound holds and yields exactly the theorem's stated |1-ℓ^2|^((q+1)^T).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (d+1)^T with (q+1)^T in the two exponent occurrences of the proof's inequality chain so that the intermediate bound matches the known Padé error rate and the theorem statement.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of theorem:convergence is invalid as written. The super-exponential rate and the claimed quadratic/cubic orders for d = 3 and d = 5 are not established by the given argument, though the theorem statement itself is correct.
issues.title: Convergence proof uses wrong exponent in Padé error bound
issues.why_classification: A single substitution of the exponent makes the proof match the already-correct theorem statement. No new lemma, construction, or argument is needed; every claim and guarantee survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: When ℓ = u the interval [ℓ,u] is a single point. For d ≥ 3 the minimax problem has infinitely many minimizers (any odd p with p(ℓ) = 1 gives zero error), so the uniqueness claim is false. The equioscillation characterization requires q+2 ≥ 3 distinct points in a one-point set, which is impossible. Chebyshev's theorem is invoked outside its hypotheses because the approximation set lacks enough points.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis ℓ < u to theorem:approxtheorystuff, and handle the degenerate case ℓ = u with a one-line argument in the proofs of lemma:computableerror and theorem:greedy.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness and equioscillation claims of theorem:approxtheorystuff are false for ℓ = u. The proofs of lemma:computableerror and theorem:greedy have a gap at ℓ = u because they invoke the equioscillation property, although both results remain true there by trivial arguments.
issues.title: Equioscillation lemma omits hypothesis ℓ < u
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local condition (ℓ < u) and a trivial degenerate-case remark preserves every substantive claim, rate, and scope with no new lemma or replacement argument.

issues.failure_explanation: With E₀ = ∞ and E₋₁ = −∞, the while-loop guard evaluates ||E₀| − |E₋₁|| = |∞ − ∞|, which is undefined (NaN in IEEE 754). Since NaN > ε is false, the loop body never executes and the algorithm returns coefficients a_k, b_k, c_k that were never computed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the initialization so the loop-guard is well-defined on entry, e.g. set E₋₁ = 0 instead of −∞, or use a Boolean flag for the first iteration.
issues.overall_effect: Algorithm alg:remezdeg5 is non-functional as written: it returns undefined polynomial coefficients whenever ℓ/u < 1 − ε^(1/3). The Python implementation in app:code handles the initialization correctly and is unaffected.
issues.title: Remez algorithm initialization prevents main loop from executing
issues.why_classification: A one-line change to the initialization values makes the algorithm well-defined and fully operational; no algorithmic logic, convergence property, or output guarantee changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then we construct the unique odd cubic polynomial $p(x) = ax + bx^3$ that satisfies $p(\sqrt{1-z^2})=1$ and $p(z) = 1$ by setting
By minimizing $p(1)$ over all valid $z$s (that is, over the interval $[1/\sqrt{2}, 1]$), one can further show that $p(1) > 1/\sqrt{2}$

issues.failure_explanation: The denominator z √(1−z²)(2z²−1) vanishes at z = 1/√2 (where 2z²−1 = 0) and at z = 1 (where √(1−z²) = 0). At z = 1 the condition p(√(1−z²)) = p(0) = 1 is incompatible with p(0) = 0 for odd polynomials, so no solution exists. At z = 1/√2 the two interpolation conditions coincide (since √(1−z²) = z), so the solution is not unique. The claims of a unique odd cubic and of minimization over the closed interval [1/√2, 1] fail at the endpoints.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the construction to z ∈ (1/√2, 1) (open interval) and replace the minimization claim with an infimum or limit statement at the endpoints; alternatively add hypotheses excluding the boundary values.
issues.overall_effect: The spectrum-aware initialization construction is ill-defined at z = 1/√2 and z = 1. The uniqueness claim and the minimization over [1/√2, 1] are unsupported at these boundary values. The main Polar Express method does not use this construction.
issues.title: Spectrum-aware initialization polynomial undefined at boundary parameter values
issues.why_classification: Restricting the parameter range to the open interval and restating the minimization as an infimum preserves the construction and the claim p(1) > 1/√2 for all valid z; this is a routine degenerate-case fix with no loss of substance.
